matches.quote: The abstract says STT in AFMTJs "has been assumed non-existent". The paper itself cites theoretical predictions of spin-transfer torque in noncollinear antiferromagnetic junctions (refs. 44–46, 60).
Spin-orbit torque from in-plane current in the Pt seed and capping layers near the pillar. The group's own earlier work (ref. 13) switches PtMn3 by SOT from Pt.
Discuss why a junction with an amorphous barrier and polycrystalline electrodes would exceed the TMR of epitaxial Mn3Pt AFMTJs (ref. 12)
All layers were deposited at room temperature without annealing (Methods), which usually gives a chemically disordered A1 phase with a different magnetic structure.
Fig. 2b shows that most of the 36 devices have TMR below about 100%. The 363% value comes from a single device
The NV sample (Extended Data Fig. 2) is a co-sputtered, epitaxial (100) PtMn3 film on an MgO(100) substrate... The domain sizes it gives cannot be carried over
Fig. 2c has four temperatures (300, 330, 360, 400 K) on one device... Provide a finer temperature series (Jc(T) and TMR(T)) on several devices
The inference that only pillars smaller than about 100–170 nm switch abruptly is not borne out by Extended Data Fig. 1, where... some 50–75 nm pillars switch gradually.
Bipolar, reversible, multilevel resistance switching with large on/off ratios is the signature of oxygen-vacancy or filamentary resistive switching in thin oxides.
the paper does not report: the number of consecutive cycles per device; switching probability versus pulse amplitude
There is no field-driven R(H) loop showing that the same high and low resistance levels can be reached with a magnetic field
The T1 noncollinear octupole state... belong to chemically ordered L12 Mn3Pt near the 3:1 composition... Provide the composition (EDS/RBS/XPS).
Reading the two fitted lines in Fig. 2d gives... Δ ≈ 25–30 for AP→P and Δ ≈ 45–55 for P→AP... The large asymmetry is not discussed.
Devices in Fig. 2 are not identified... whether devices degrade or break down after repeated multi-volt pulses.

notes: C16 and C18 are already addressed in the v1 text (p. 5 states STEM was performed on 200 nm pillars; p. 10 includes a paragraph speculating on band-structure and chemical strategies to enhance OTT). C11 is partly matched by P2 (asks for T-series on several devices across 360 K, but not cooling reversibility). C12 is partly matched by P23 (asks for layer stoichiometry, though not whether single-target or co-sputtering was used for the device stack). C15 is partly matched by P6/P10 (discusses polarity asymmetry in Fig. 2d rather than Fig. 2a). P3 and P13 are duplicate points in the provided list.
